shouldFix.title: ID-DEP-S5 gives six upstream rows the register token OPEN when all six are HARD-BLOCKED - erasing the very property DR-109's own status says it inherits
shouldFix.subjectQuote: 'DR-002 through DR-008 leftovers still OPEN or PARTIALLY SATISFIED'

measurement.soTheClaimIsRightForOneOfSeven: Only DR-008 matches. Six of seven are HARD-BLOCKED, and none of those six is OPEN.
measurement.theTokensAreDistinctInThisRegister: I censused the status column across every DR row: OPEN appears 19 times, HARD-BLOCKED 9 times, PARTIALLY SATISFIED once, alongside SATISFIED, ACCEPTED, DECIDED-V*, PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW and RELEASE-QUALIFICATION-ONLY. OPEN and HARD-BLOCKED co-exist as separate tokens; one is not shorthand for the other.
measurement.theArtifactUsesTokenVocabularyDeliberate: 'PARTIALLY SATISFIED' is capitalised exactly as the register writes it, so this field is quoting register tokens rather than speaking loosely - which is what makes the six wrong ones wrong.

shouldFix.why: DR-109's own status, which this artifact quotes verbatim and repeats in authorityClaim, is 'OPEN / inherits hard blockers'. What it inherits hard blockers FROM is precisely DR-002 through DR-007. Describing those six as OPEN deletes the property that explains DR-109's own standing, and understates how far the applied evidence successor named in the row's acceptance cell actually is from being available.
shouldFix.whatIsNotWrongWithIt: The stated consequence - 'Exact records remain reserved. This artifact does not close those rows.' - is true and unaffected. The defect is the status characterisation, not the dependency or its effect.
shouldFix.severityReasoning: SHOULD-FIX. It is an accuracy defect in a recorded dependency rather than an authority escape, and this corpus has consistently graded inaccurate register/version characterisations at this level rather than as blockers.
shouldFix.fix: Restate as 'DR-002 through DR-007 HARD-BLOCKED and DR-008 PARTIALLY SATISFIED', or use a token-neutral phrase such as 'not closed'. Either removes the mismatch without changing the dependency.

observations.title: Two fields carry standing LIVE for COORD, while one of them says it is the only such claim
observations.detail: reMeasurementAtV1.note reads 'This is the only this-generation live COORD claim (standing LIVE)', but recordedInputs.governingSources[2] also carries standing 'LIVE' with role 'This pin is this-generation live' for the same file. Strictly there are two LIVE claims, so 'the only' is inaccurate. Not filed as a finding because both carry the identical digest 0833973f... and the identical head, so nothing is ambiguous and no reader can be misled about which value is current. Worth tightening if this family grows remeasurement blocks the way the DR-101 family did, where multiple stale blocks each reading 'Live remasurement' became a real hazard.

observations.title: The mid-sentence carry boundary is disclosed rather than hidden
observations.detail: The carry of file 04 lines 38-58 ends on 'architecture does', with the sentence completing on line 59. The artifact records sourceContinuityLine59: 'not invent them.', which I verified is byte-identical to live line 59. A carry that stops mid-sentence is exactly where a reader could be misled about what the source concedes; disclosing the completion is the honest handling and is worth recording as done right.

summary: The extraction itself is clean and I checked it against the sources rather than against its own description. Both carries are byte-exact - the 21 lines of file 04 38-58 and the state-class row at 202 - and the carry that stops mid-sentence discloses its completion on line 59, which I verified. The DR-109 row reproduces byte-exact at line 291 and all seven acceptance-cell fragments decompose faithfully. Most importantly for this row, nothing invents a commit, CAS, ledger, path or backend API: the interface block is carried language plus explicit refusals, and storage is never allowed to become an evidence writer or a second authority. Failure modes are carried verbatim, and the one addition to the source's deferral list - DR-113 - is grounded in that row's own acceptance cell. No D-096 (A) grant, no SATISFIED claim, and the dispatch's D-106/DR-103 caveat is honoured explicitly. One defect stops it. ID-DEP-S5 says the DR-002 through DR-008 leftovers are 'still OPEN or PARTIALLY SATISFIED'. Measured against the register, six of those seven rows are HARD-BLOCKED and only DR-008 is PARTIALLY SATISFIED; a census of the status column shows OPEN and HARD-BLOCKED are distinct co-existing tokens, and the field is quoting token vocabulary deliberately. That matters here more than it would elsewhere: DR-109's own status is 'OPEN / inherits hard blockers', and the six rows described as OPEN are exactly what it inherits those hard blockers from. The dependency and its consequence are sound; only the status words are wrong, and restating them closes it. Separately, COORD advanced two commits after the subject was frozen; I tested the PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT conditions individually - append-only delta, file 08 and file 04 unchanged, subject unmoved, and the pin reproducing from git at its stated HEAD - and all hold, so nothing is charged for it.
